summary: Built a redundant transit topology between node1 (VyOS) and node2 (OPNsense), each serving a private network (node3, node4 respectively), so node3 and node4 keep reaching each other across either of the two independent transit links. Discovered the physical wiring via STP bridge-ID correlation (node1 eth1<->node2 vtnet1 = Transit A; node1 eth2<->node2 vtnet2 = Transit B; node1 eth3<->node3 enp8s0 = Private-A; node2 vtnet3<->node4 enp8s0 = Private-B). Configured VyOS with an ECMP static route (two next-hops, each pinned to its own interface to avoid FRR's recursive-via-default fallback when a link drops) and OPNsense with two monitored gateways (GW_T1/GW_T2) in a gateway group compiled into a pf 'route-to' rule for node4-initiated traffic, plus a real FreeBSD multipath kernel route (net.route.multipath=1, persisted via config.xml sysctl + an rc.syshook boot script) to correctly handle the reverse/asymmetric path for node3-initiated traffic. Validated failover live: started a continuous ping from node3 to node4, administratively disabled node1's eth1 (Transit A), watched OPNsense's dpinger mark GW_T1 down and the pf rule auto-recompile to the single surviving path, observed ~41 dropped pings during the ~45s convergence window, then confirmed the ping stream resumed and continued successfully — demonstrating continuity across the transition. Re-enabled eth1 and confirmed both gateways returned online and ECMP was restored on both routers. Completed the mandatory node-restart protocol: captured a pre-restart boot identity and health baseline for all four nodes, then restarted node1, node2, node3, and node4 one at a time (never overlapping), polled each until exec was available again, proved each node's boot identity changed, and verified post-restart that all addressing, routes, gateway health, and end-to-end node3<->node4 connectivity fully recovered (catching and permanently fixing a boot-time race on node2 where only one of the two multipath routes was reinstalled).
actions_performed: Inspected all 4 nodes' OS/interfaces and used STP bridge-ID correlation across tcpdump captures to determine actual point-to-point wiring between node1, node2, node3, node4
Addressed VyOS (node1) interfaces eth1/eth2/eth3 and configured an ECMP static route to 10.10.20.0/24 with two interface-pinned next-hops

Addressed Ubuntu nodes 3 and 4 via dedicated systemd-networkd .network files (10-enp8s0.network) to avoid the 50-all-interfaces.network DHCP reconciler, including static routes to the peer private subnet

Edited OPNsense (node2) config.xml via Python/ElementTree to add opt1/opt2/opt3 interfaces, gateway_item GW_T1/GW_T2, a gateway_group TRANSIT_GRP, and firewall pass rules (including policy-routing via the gateway group on opt3)

Applied OPNsense config via configctl interface reconfigure / interface routes configure / filter reload; diagnosed and fixed an asymmetric-routing gap for node3-initiated flows by enabling net.route.multipath and adding real FreeBSD multipath kernel routes, persisted via config.xml sysctl entry and a new rc.syshook.d/start script

Ran a live failover test: continuous ping from node3, disabled node1 eth1, observed automatic OPNsense gateway-group failover and dropped-then-recovered ping stream, re-enabled eth1 and confirmed full ECMP/gateway recovery

Executed the mandatory node-restart evidence protocol: captured boot_id/kern.boottime baselines, rebooted node1, node2, node3, node4 sequentially (one at a time), polled each back online, proved changed boot identity for each, and re-verified configuration persistence and node3<->node4 connectivity after every restart
Found and fixed a node2 boot-time gap where only one multipath route was reinstalled after reboot, by adding a persistent rc.syshook script
